intro.title: Quick orientation
intro.body: FiveByFive is a free trainer for the NATO phonetic alphabet. Practice letters, radio phrases and callsign spelling without an account. Your progress is saved locally in your browser, and you can change themes and fonts at any time.

footer.title: Still stuck?
footer.body: If something feels off, it is usually one of two things: a set that is too large, or a mode that does not match your goal. Use the links below to reset your setup in under a minute.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.description: What FiveByFive is, how it works, and what you should do first.

q1.question: What is FiveByFive?
q1.answer: FiveByFive is a free trainer for the NATO phonetic alphabet. It teaches the ICAO code word for every letter, radio phrases used in voice communication, and spelling words with code words.

q2.question: Is FiveByFive really free?
q2.answer: Yes. FiveByFive is free to use with no required account and no paywalled training content.

q3.question: Do I need to create an account?
q3.answer: No. Your preferences and statistics are stored locally in your browser. If you clear site data or switch devices, your local progress will not follow you.

learningPath.title: Suggested order
learningPath.description: A practical order for learning the phonetic alphabet.

q1.question: Should I learn letters or radio phrases first?
q1.answer: Start with the letters A to Z so every code word is familiar. Then move to radio codes and phrases, and finish with spelling full words and callsigns.

q2.question: How long does it take to learn the code words?
q2.answer: Short daily sessions work best. Most learners get comfortable with the alphabet within a couple of weeks, then keep improving speed with Blitz drills.

q3.question: When should I start spelling words?
q3.answer: Once you can match letters to code words without hesitating, start spelling short words. Spelling practice reinforces the same code words in a different context.

features.title: Features & training modes
features.description: How practice works and which mode to pick for your goal.

q1.question: What are the training modes?
q1.answer: FiveByFive includes recognition and recall modes (pick/reverse-pick, input/reverse-input) plus timed Blitz challenges and full-set Gauntlet runs. Switch modes depending on whether you want accuracy, recall, or speed.

q2.question: What is the best mode for beginners?
q2.answer: Start with pick mode to build fast recognition, then add input mode for typing recall. Alternating the two works well for code words and spelling.

q3.question: Can I customize themes and fonts?
q3.answer: Yes. FiveByFive supports themes, fonts and display preferences so long practice sessions stay comfortable.

privacy.title: Privacy & data
privacy.description: What is stored, where it is stored, and what that means for you.

q1.question: Where is my progress saved?
q1.answer: Your progress is saved locally in your browser. Statistics stay on your device and you can start training without signing up.

q2.question: Will my progress sync across devices?
q2.answer: Not automatically. Progress is stored locally, so switching browsers or devices will not carry it over unless you move the data yourself.

q3.question: Does FiveByFive work offline?
q3.answer: Core practice can work offline once assets are cached, but the first load and any network-backed features need a connection.

jlpt.title: Training tiers
jlpt.description: How the five tiers are organized.

q1.question: What are the five tiers?
q1.answer: Codes and Spelling are split into five tiers. Tier 1 holds the most common items and Tier 5 holds the most demanding ones. You can select any tier directly.

q2.question: Do I need to finish a tier before the next one?
q2.answer: No. The tiers are a way to keep practice sets manageable. Pick the tier that matches your current accuracy and move on when it feels easy.

q3.question: What should I practice first?
q3.answer: Start with letters A to Z, then Tier 1 radio codes. After that, spell short words and review the items you miss most often.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.description: Fix the most common ‘why am I not improving?’ problems.

q1.question: I keep mixing up similar code words. What should I do?
q1.answer: Reduce your active set and drill recognition first. Confusable pairs such as B and D or M and N deserve their own short sessions.

q2.question: My accuracy is fine but I am slow.
q2.answer: Add timed practice with a small set. Speed usually improves once accuracy is stable.

q3.question: My progress looks reset. Did I lose everything?
q3.answer: Progress is stored locally. Clearing browser data, using private mode, or switching devices can make it look reset. Check that you are in the same browser profile and that site data is not being cleared automatically.
